mainTopic: Business with those going to or from idol festivals and fairs, and making gentile wine containers usable
overview: The amud opens by explaining that a Jew coming back from an idol festival (תרפות) is a problem because he has become attached to it and will go again. רב אשי limits a ברייתא that forbids him even on the way there to a מומר, who will surely go. A second ברייתא about a fair (יריד) permits business with a גוי both ways, but forbids it with a Jew on the way back, because his trip shows he went to sell idol items. ריש לקיש then limits the משנה's permission for those returning from a festival to people who are not traveling as a group. The גמרא turns to gentile wineskins: רב פפא and רב זביד each explain a ברייתא about a גוי tarring them, and רב אשי rejects רב פפי's extension to wine thrown into salt. A story about רב יצחק בר יוסף teaches that wineskins can be made usable by soaking them in water for three days, changing the water every twenty-four hours. This method works for ours and theirs, and for wineskins and jugs alike. A final ברייתא sums up the rules for gentile jugs, and a new question is opened that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why a Jew coming back from an idol festival is a problem
steps.stepSummary: The reasoning just given is completed: a Jew who went to an idol festival has become attached to it and will go back again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he has become attached to it, he will go back to it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation from just before: why we may not do business with a Jew who is returning from an idol festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the way there, a Jew might still change his mind, so business with him is allowed. But once he has actually gone, he is attached to it. Doing business with him now would help him go back again.

phrases.english: Since he has cleaved to it,
phrases.notes: This finishes the reasoning from just before: "he" is a Jew coming back from the idol festival.

phrases.english: he will go back to it again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning begun before this section about a Jew returning from an idol festival.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew returning from an idol festival is forbidden for business, since he is now attached and will go again.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids business with a Jew even on the way there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that forbids business with a Jew going to an idol festival both going and returning, which goes against allowing it on the way there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: a Jew who goes to an idol festival, whether on the way there or on the way back, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that business with a Jew on his way to the festival is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view split the cases: going is allowed, because he may change his mind, and returning is forbidden. This ברייתא forbids both, so it seems to reject the idea that a Jew might change his mind.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
a Jew who goes to an idol festival,
whether going or returning, it is forbidden!
phrases.notes: "Forbidden" here means it is forbidden to do business with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view that a Jew on the way to the festival is permitted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission to do business with a Jew who is on his way to an idol festival.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids business even while he is going, so it does not accept that he might change his mind.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא is about a מומר
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the ברייתא is talking about a Jew who is a מומר, who will certainly go, so even on the way there it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That ברייתא is talking about a Jew who is a מומר, who will certainly go.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא speaks about a different kind of Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason a regular Jew is allowed on the way there is that he might change his mind. A מומר is already set on idol worship, so we do not expect him to turn back. Both rules can stand: regular Jew going is allowed, and a מומר is forbidden both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jew who has left Torah observance (a מומר)

steps.whatToRemember: A regular Jew on the way to the festival might change his mind, so it is allowed. A מומר will surely go, so it is forbidden both going and returning.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When that was taught, it was about an apostate Jew,
who will certainly go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by limiting the ברייתא to a מומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (the ברייתא speaks of a different type of person)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about any Jew, which would mean no Jew is trusted to change his mind.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks only of a מומר, who will certainly go; a regular Jew on the way may still change his mind.

steps.title: A ברייתא about going to a fair
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: business with a גוי going to or returning from a fair is allowed; with a Jew, going is allowed but returning is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a גוי who goes to a fair, both going and returning, it is permitted. A Jew who goes to a fair, going it is permitted, returning it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a fair, and it sets up a surprising difference between a Jew and a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fair, not an idol festival, so the rules differ. The surprise is that the Jew is treated more strictly than the גוי on the way back. The next steps will ask why.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
a gentile who goes to a fair,
whether going or returning, it is permitted.
A Jew who goes to a fair,
going, it is permitted,
returning, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic: a fair instead of an idol festival.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי going to or from a fair is permitted; a Jew is permitted going but forbidden returning.

steps.title: Why is the Jew forbidden on the way back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes a Jew returning from the fair different, so that business with him is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a Jew, that on the way back it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the strict rule for a Jew coming back from the fair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule but not the reason. The question is especially sharp because the גוי, who we would expect to be treated more strictly, is permitted.

phrases.english: What is different about a Jew
that on the way back it is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's ruling on a Jew returning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a Jew returning from the fair is forbidden for business.

steps.title: He probably sold idol items
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we assume he sold idol items at the fair, so the money he now holds is money from עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we say: he sold idol items, so money from עבודה זרה is with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the strict rule: the Jew's money is probably from selling idol items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not that he will go back to idol worship. The problem is the money itself: money gained from selling עבודה זרה is forbidden, so doing business with him means getting that money.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this reason with the idol festival reason. There the worry was that he would go back; here the worry is the forbidden money he is holding.

phrases.english: Because we say:
he sold idol items,
so money from idol worship is with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Jew is assumed to have sold idol items, so he holds forbidden money from עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Why not say the same about the גוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the same reasoning should apply to a גוי returning from the fair, who may also have sold idol items.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a גוי too, let us say: he sold idol items, so money from עבודה זרה is with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer, saying it should forbid the גוי as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason is that the money may come from selling idols, a גוי is even more likely to have sold them. Yet the ברייתא permits the גוי both ways, so the reason seems not to fit.

phrases.english: For a gentile too, let us say:
he sold idol items,
so money from idol worship is with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6 using the ruling on the גוי from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that a Jew returning holds money from selling idol items.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same worry applies to a גוי, yet the ברייתא permits business with him even on the way back.

steps.title: A gentile probably sold ordinary goods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 7. About a גוי coming back from the fair, we assume he sold ordinary things like a cloak or wine, not idol items.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, about a gentile we say: he sold a cloak, he sold wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why a גוי returning from the fair is permitted. We assume he sold normal goods there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 asked why we don't suspect the גוי of selling idol items, the same as the Jew. The answer is that for a גוי we give the easy assumption that he sold ordinary goods, so his money is not money of עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: Rather, regarding a gentile, we say:
he sold a cloak, he sold wine;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גוי returning from the fair should be suspected just like the Jew
steps.terutzMaskana: For a גוי we assume he sold ordinary goods like a cloak or wine

steps.title: Why not assume the same about the Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if we assume the גוי sold ordinary goods, we should assume the same about the Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a Jew too, let us say: assume he sold a cloak, he sold wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The same kind assumption should work for the Jew too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we can assume a גוי sold ordinary goods, there seems to be no reason to treat a Jew worse. That would mean business with the returning Jew should also be permitted, which goes against the ברייתא.

phrases.english: For a Jew too, let us say:
Assume he sold a cloak, he sold wine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that returning with a Jew is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The kind assumption used for the גוי should apply equally to the Jew

steps.title: A Jew could have sold ordinary goods at home
steps.stepSummary: If the Jew only had ordinary goods, he would have sold them here at home. His trip to the fair shows he went to sell idol items.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had ordinary goods, he would have sold them here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the Jew is different. The fact that he bothered to travel to the fair shows he had something to sell there that he couldn't sell at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary goods can be sold anywhere, so a Jew with only clothing or wine had no need to go to the gentiles' fair. His going there points to selling idol items, so his money is treated as money of עבודה זרה. This closes the question from Step 5.
steps.whatToRemember: A גוי returning from the fair is assumed to have sold ordinary goods. A Jew is assumed to have sold idol items, because he could have sold ordinary goods at home.

phrases.english: If it were so that he had it here,
phrases.notes: He means: if the Jew only had a cloak or wine, things he could sell right here at home.

phrases.english: he would have sold it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Jew might also have sold ordinary goods
steps.terutzMaskana: The Jew's trip to the fair shows he went to sell idol items

steps.title: Those coming back are permitted only if not traveling together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that גוים coming back from an idol festival (תרפות) are permitted for business. ריש לקיש limits it to people who are not traveling as a group.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: those coming back are permitted. רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: this is only when they are not tied to one another, but if they are tied to one another, it is forbidden, because I say he plans to go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and brings ריש לקיש, who adds a limit to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה permits business with גוים returning from an idol festival. ריש לקיש says this is only when they come back separately. If they are traveling together as a group, we worry that the גוי plans to go back to the festival with his friends, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And those who are coming back
Tied to one another, meaning traveling together as a group
His plan is to go back

phrases.english: And those who are coming back are permitted.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה, about גוים coming back from an idol festival.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין קְשׁוּרִין זֶה בָּזֶה,
phrases.english: They taught this only where they are not tied to one another,
but if they are tied to one another, it is forbidden,
for I say his intention is to go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַבָּאִין מוּתָּרִין. אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those returning from an idol festival are permitted only when they are not traveling as a group. If they are, it is forbidden, because they may be going back.

steps.title: A ברייתא about gentile wineskins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about gentile wineskins and jugs and brings a ברייתא. New stripped wineskins are permitted and old tarred ones are forbidden. If a גוי tarred and lined them and put wine in while a Jew stood over him, there is no concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: wineskins of gentiles and their jugs. The רבנן taught: gentile wineskins that are stripped and new are permitted. Old and tarred ones are forbidden. If a gentile tarred them, lined them, and put wine in them while a Jew stood over him, he need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא with the details of when gentile wineskins may be used. The last line of the ברייתא sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes a split. New wineskins with no tar are fine, and old tarred ones are forbidden. Then it adds a case where a גוי prepared the wineskins and put wine into them while a Jew watched, and says this is fine. That last case will look strange to the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: He tarred them and lined them

phrases.english: Wineskins of gentiles and their jugs.
phrases.notes: This quotes the next line of our משנה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: wineskins of gentiles,
if stripped and new, they are permitted,
if old and tarred, they are forbidden.
If a gentile tarred them and lined them
and put wine into them,

phrases.aramaic: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו — אֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ.
phrases.english: and a Jew stands over him, he need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: New, stripped gentile wineskins are permitted and old tarred ones are forbidden. A גוי preparing them with a Jew standing over him is no concern.

steps.title: What does the watching Jew help?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the גוי himself put the wine in, what difference does it make that a Jew was standing over him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the gentile puts wine into them, what difference does it make that a Jew stands over him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the last case of the ברייתא. A Jew watching does not seem to change anything once the גוי handled the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is the גוי putting wine in, not whether someone saw it. A Jew standing there does not undo the fact that the גוי handled the wine. So the ruling "he need not worry" seems hard to understand.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּגוֹי נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָן יַיִן,
phrases.english: But since the gentile puts wine into them,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: what difference does it make that a Jew stands over him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּגוֹי נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָן יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last case of the ברייתא in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a Jew standing over the גוי removes the concern
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the גוי himself put the wine in, a Jew watching cannot fix the problem

steps.title: רב פפא: A Jew put the wine in
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא re-reads the ברייתא. The גוי only tarred and lined the wineskins, a Jew put the wine in, and another Jew stood over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this is what it means: a gentile tarred and lined them, a Jew put wine into them, and another Jew stood over him, and he need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers by explaining the ברייתא differently. The גוי never touched the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב פפא's reading, the גוי's job ends after tarring and lining. A Jew is the one who puts the wine in, while another Jew watches. Since the wine was handled only by Jews, the question from Step 13 disappears.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying that watching a גוי pour wine makes it permitted. He changes the case so that a Jew does the pouring.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, the גוי only prepared the containers and a Jew put the wine in. רב זביד in step 17 offers a different reading, where the גוי pours.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This is what it means:
a gentile tarred them and lined them,
and a Jew puts wine into them,
and another Jew stands over him,
and he need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גוי put the wine in and the Jew only watched
steps.terutzMaskana: The גוי only prepared the wineskins, a Jew put the wine in, and another Jew stood over him

steps.title: Why need a second Jew if a Jew pours the wine?
steps.stepSummary: On רב פפא's reading, a Jew pours the wine. So why does the ברייתא also need another Jew standing over him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since a Jew is the one putting the wine in, why do I need another Jew standing over him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's new reading from Step 14. If a Jew does the pouring, a second Jew watching seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא moved the pouring from the גוי to a Jew to explain why a watcher matters. But now the watcher looks unnecessary, because a Jew pouring should already protect the wine.

phrases.english: But since a Jew is the one putting wine into them,

phrases.aramaic: יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֵר עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: why do I need another Jew standing over him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָן יַיִן, יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֵר עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's reading from Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading that a Jew pours and another Jew watches
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Jew pouring should be enough protection, so the second Jew seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The pourer may be too busy to notice
steps.stepSummary: The second Jew is needed because the pourer, busy with his work, might not notice the גוי libating the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps, while the Jew is busy pouring, the גוי will libate the wine, and the Jew will not be aware of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The Jew who pours is focused on his job, so a second Jew must watch the גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pourer is present but distracted. The watcher's only job is to keep an eye on the גוי, so רב פפא's reading still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Pours wine as an offering to an idol (libation)
In his awareness; noticed by him

phrases.english: Perhaps, because of his being busy, he (the גוי) will libate,
phrases.notes: "His being busy" refers to the Jew who is pouring. The one who libates is the גוי.

phrases.english: and it will not be in his (the Jew's) awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the practical role of the second Jew
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A Jew pouring the wine is enough supervision
steps.terutzMaskana: The pourer is distracted, so a separate watcher is needed to guard against libation.

steps.title: רב זביד: the גוי pours, but it is like splashing water into mud
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד keeps the original reading that the גוי pours the wine. He explains that pouring wine into freshly tarred skins is like throwing water into clay, so the גוי does not mean it as a libation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: Really, it is as you first said, that the גוי pours. When he pours the wine in, he is like someone throwing water into mud.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד offers a different answer to Step 13's question. He does not change the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד agrees that the גוי pours. The pouring itself is not a concern, because wine poured into fresh tar is being treated like something thrown away, not offered. The watching Jew is there for the time after the pouring.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; in truth (keeps the original reading)
Like throwing water into clay or mud

steps.confusionAlert: רב זביד is not arguing with Step 16. He goes back to Step 13 and answers it differently, keeping the ברייתא exactly as written.

phrases.english: רב זביד said:
Really, it is as you said at first,
phrases.notes: "At first" means the plain reading of the ברייתא from Step 12, where the גוי himself puts the wine in.

phrases.english: and here, at the moment that he throws it in,
he is considered like one throwing water into clay.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כִּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to Step 13, instead of רב פפא's reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: Keeps the text and redefines the act of pouring
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי pouring wine automatically raises a libation concern
steps.terutzMaskana: Pouring into fresh tar is like throwing water into mud, with no libation intent at that moment.

steps.title: רב פפי: wine a גוי throws into a Jew's salt is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי draws a conclusion from רב זביד: if a גוי threw wine into a Jew's salt container, the salt is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: Learn from רב זביד that if a גוי threw wine into a Jew's salt container, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי takes רב זביד's idea and applies it to a new case. This sets up רב אשי's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפי understands רב זביד to mean that wine thrown into something else is not a libation. So wine a גוי tosses into salt should not forbid the salt.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; conclude from it

phrases.english: רב פפי said:
Learn from the statement of רב זביד
that this גוי who threw wine
into a Jew's salt container: it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפֵּי: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַב זְבִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב זביד's principle to a new case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew's salt is permitted if a גוי threw wine into it, because there is no libation intent.

steps.title: רב אשי: the cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects רב פפי's comparison. In the tarred skin, the wine goes to waste. In the salt, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: Are they comparable? There the wine goes to waste. Here it does not go to waste.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רב פפי's inference. רב זביד's idea does not carry over to the salt case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring into fresh tar is like splashing into mud only because the wine is being lost. Wine in salt is not lost, so the גוי's act there could still count, and the salt is not automatically permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Is going to waste; being lost

steps.whatToRemember: רב זביד's principle only works where the wine is going to waste. It does not extend to wine poured into salt.

phrases.english: רב אשי objects to it:
Are they comparable?
There, it is going to waste,
phrases.notes: "There" is the wine poured into the freshly tarred wineskin.

phrases.english: here, it is not going to waste.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפי's inference in Step 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the extension to the salt case, not רב זביד's principle itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The tarred-skin case depends on the wine going to waste, which is not true of salt.

steps.title: A גוי seizes רב יצחק בר יוסף's wineskins
steps.stepSummary: בר עדי, an Arab, took רב יצחק בר יוסף's wineskins, put wine in them, and gave them back. רב יצחק בר יוסף went to ask the בית מדרש what to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר עדי the Arab seized some wineskins from רב יצחק בר יוסף, put wine in them, and returned them to him. He came and asked in the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story that raises a practical question. This sets up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wineskins have now absorbed a גוי's wine. The question is how to make them usable again for a Jew.

phrases.english: בר עדי the Arab

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַס הָנְהוּ זִיקֵי מֵרַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: seized certain wineskins from רב יצחק בר יוסף,
put wine in them,
and returned them to him.
He came and asked in the study hall.
phrases.notes: "He" is רב יצחק בר יוסף, asking how to make his wineskins usable again.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר עֲדִי טַיָּיעָא אֲנַס הָנְהוּ זִיקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of gentile wineskins with a real case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a practical question about wineskins a גוי filled with wine.

steps.title: Fill them with water for three days
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes רבי אמי's practical ruling: fill the wineskins with water for three days, then pour it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to him: This is how רבי אמי ruled in practice. One fills them with water for three days and pours it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question from the story with a ruling he received from רבי אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water soaks up the absorbed wine over three days. Pouring it out removes the forbidden wine, so the wineskins become usable.

phrases.english: רבי ירמיה said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הוֹרָה רַבִּי אַמֵּי הֲלָכָה לְמַעֲשֶׂה —
phrases.english: This is how רבי אמי ruled as practical halacha:
one fills them with water for three days
and pours them out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: כָּךְ הוֹרָה רַבִּי אַמֵּי הֲלָכָה לְמַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in the story
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to make wineskins usable after a גוי filled them with wine
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fill them with water for three days and then pour it out.

steps.title: רבא: change the water every twenty-four hours
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that the water must be poured out every twenty-four hours during the three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: One must pour them out every twenty-four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a detail to רבי אמי's ruling about how the three-day soaking works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough to leave the same water in for three days. The water is emptied and refilled each full day, three times in all.
steps.whatToRemember: Wineskins a גוי filled with wine are made usable by soaking them in water for three days, changing the water every twenty-four hours.

phrases.english: And רבא said:
One must pour them out every twenty-four hours.
phrases.notes: "Pour them out" means empty the water and refill, so fresh water soaks the skins each day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: צָרִיךְ לְעָרָן מֵעֵת לְעֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to רבי אמי's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The water must be emptied and replaced every twenty-four hours during the three days.

steps.title: First assumption: the water method only works for our wineskins
steps.stepSummary: The scholars first understood that רבי אמי's three-day water method applies only to Jewish wineskins that a gentile used, not to wineskins that belong to gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: it applies only to our wineskins, but not to theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how people first understood רבי אמי's ruling: it only helps for a Jew's own wineskins. This sets up the next step, which will correct this assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story, the wineskins belonged to רב יצחק בר יוסף and a gentile seized them and used them for his wine. So people assumed the leniency depends on that, and that a gentile's own wineskins, used for his wine all along, cannot be fixed this way.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (a first assumption, often corrected later)
This applies only to... (limits a rule)

phrases.english: They understood from it:
phrases.notes: "It" is רבי אמי's ruling to fill the wineskins with water for three days.

phrases.english: this applies only to ours,
phrases.notes: "Ours" means Jewish wineskins that a gentile used, like in the story.

phrases.english: but theirs — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a limiting assumption from the ruling of רבי אמי and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Assumed: the three-day water method works only for Jewish-owned wineskins.

steps.title: רבין reports: the method works for both ours and theirs
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings ריש לקיש's teaching from ארץ ישראל: the water method works both for Jewish wineskins and for gentile wineskins.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said that רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: both ours and theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין arrives with a teaching from רבי שמעון בן לקיש that cancels the assumption in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption had limited the leniency to Jewish containers. ריש לקיש says ownership makes no difference, so gentile wineskins can also be made permitted with the three-day water method.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a teaching)

phrases.english: When Ravin came
he said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
Both ours and theirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limiting assumption of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the 'only ours' limitation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Who owns the wineskin does not matter for the water method.
steps.whatToRemember: The three-day water method works for gentile wineskins too, not only Jewish ones.

steps.title: רב אחא suggests the method only works for leather wineskins
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא suggests to רב אשי that the water method applies only to leather wineskins, not to jugs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא thought to say before רב אשי: this applies only to wineskins, but not to jugs.
steps.whatsHappening: A second possible limit is suggested, this time about the type of container. This sets up רב אשי's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 settled that ownership does not matter. Now רב אחא asks if the material matters: maybe the method works for leather wineskins but not for clay jugs.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say (a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: Rav Aha son of Rava thought
to say before Rav Ashi:
This applies only to wineskins,
but jugs — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new possible limit on the water method, based on type of container.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested: the water method works only for wineskins, not jugs.

steps.title: רב אשי: wineskins and jugs are the same
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the suggestion: the water method works for both wineskins and jugs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: there is no difference between wineskins and jugs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי turns down רב אחא's suggested limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as ownership made no difference in step 24, the type of container makes no difference here. Both wineskins and jugs can be made permitted with the three-day water method.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא נוֹדוֹת וְלָא שְׁנָא קַנְקַנִּים.
phrases.english: No difference between wineskins and jugs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limit suggested in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the 'only wineskins' limitation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The type of container does not change the water method.
steps.whatToRemember: The water method works for every case discussed: ours or theirs, wineskins or jugs.

steps.title: A ברייתא on gentile jugs: new, old, and how to use them
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that new, scraped gentile jugs are permitted and old, tarred ones are forbidden. If a gentile put wine in them, a Jew puts water in them, or may put brine and fish-stew in them without worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Jugs of gentiles: new and scraped are permitted; old and tarred are forbidden. If a gentile puts wine in them, a Jew puts water in them. If a gentile puts wine in them, a Jew puts brine and fish-stew in them and does not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives clear rules for gentile jugs in different conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first separates jugs by condition: new and scraped is fine, old and tarred is forbidden. Then it gives two ways to deal with a jug a gentile put wine in: fill it with water, or use it for brine and fish-stew without worrying.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong fish sauce or stew
He does not need to worry

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Jugs of gentiles:
new and scraped — permitted,
old and tarred — forbidden.
If a gentile puts wine into them —
a Jew puts water into them;
if a gentile puts wine into them —
a Jew puts brine and fish-stew into them,
and he does not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with fuller rules on gentile containers, including the water method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: New scraped gentile jugs are permitted; old tarred ones are forbidden. After a gentile's wine, a Jew may use water, or put in brine and fish-stew without worry.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'גוי נותן לתוכן יין' appears twice on purpose. Each time it opens a different option: first water, then brine and fish-stew.

steps.title: The גמרא opens a new question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that a question was asked in the בית מדרש. The question itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked of them:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to ask a new question, which begins on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula איבעיא להו means a real open question in the בית מדרש, not an attack on someone's view. The actual question appears at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them (an open question in the בית מדרש)

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא to a new open question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated; the question itself comes on the next amud.
